sources.title: 150 Years of Huntington's Disease: The Science Behind the Suffering
sources.relevance: primary — comprehensive mechanistic synthesis: polyQ aggregation, BDNF-REST axis, CBP/transcriptional dysregulation, excitotoxicity, somatic CAG instability, therapeutic overview
sources.key_finding: Mutant huntingtin disrupts four overlapping mechanisms in MSN: BDNF supply (REST de-repression), transcriptional dysregulation (CBP/PGC-1α), excitotoxicity (NR2B NMDA, GLT1 loss), and somatic CAG expansion; nuclear inclusion toxicity remains debated

sources.title: Huntington Disease: A Single-Gene Degenerative Disorder of the Striatum
sources.relevance: primary — clinical staging, presymptomatic volumetric changes (TRACK-HD/PREDICT-HD), juvenile HD symptomology, CAG-age relationship
sources.key_finding: Structural brain changes detectable 15 years before clinical motor onset; juvenile HD (>60 CAG, ~5% of all HD) presents with rigidity/akinesia rather than chorea; mean onset 35-40 years, duration 15-20 years

sources.title: Loss of Huntingtin-Mediated BDNF Gene Transcription in Huntington's Disease
sources.relevance: landmark — establishes the wtHtt-REST-BDNF axis: wtHtt sequesters REST in cytoplasm, preventing RE1-mediated repression of BDNF promoter; mHTT loses this capacity
sources.key_finding: Wild-type huntingtin promotes BDNF transcription by sequestering REST (RE1-silencing transcription factor) in the cytoplasm; mutant huntingtin fails to sequester REST, allowing it to enter the nucleus and repress BDNF transcription via the RE1 element in BDNF exon II promoter

sources.title: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor and Huntington's disease
sources.relevance: secondary — progressive BDNF loss in multiple HD mouse models; BDNF decline precedes behavioral symptoms
sources.key_finding: Progressive BDNF reduction in cortex and striatum across multiple HD transgenic mouse models (R6/2, YAC128); BDNF decrease precedes overt behavioral phenotype and correlates with polyQ length and disease severity

sources.title: Huntington's Disease: A Clinical Review
sources.relevance: primary — clinical biomarkers (NfL, CSF mHTT), NR2B excitotoxic vulnerability, cortical late involvement, presymptomatic staging
sources.key_finding: NfL elevated in presymptomatic HD carriers; MSN NR2B-enriched NMDA receptors underlie heightened excitotoxic susceptibility; cortical neurons affected later than striatum, consistent with cortical BDNF self-sufficiency

sources.title: Therapeutic Approaches in Huntington's Disease
sources.authors: Kim A, Lalonde K, Truesdell A, Welch Estes P, Bhanu Raj P, Bhargava S, Bhargava S, Bhargava S
sources.relevance: primary — comprehensive treatment review: tetrabenazine/deutetrabenazine approval, ASO strategies, excitotoxicity (GLT1/GLAST evidence), CBP/HDAC inhibitor rationale
sources.key_finding: GLT1/GLAST downregulation in HD astrocytes contributes to impaired glutamate clearance; HDAC inhibitors restore histone acetylation and partially rescue transcriptional dysregulation; deutetrabenazine FDA-approved 2017 for chorea (VMAT2 inhibitor, does not modify disease course)

sources.title: Population pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic analysis of tominersen in patients with Huntington's disease from the phase III GENERATION HD1 study
sources.relevance: primary — tominersen PK/PD, IC50, exposure quartile analysis linking mHTT reduction to biomarker safety signal
sources.key_finding: IC50 = 4.18 ng/mL; highest exposure quartile achieved 54% mHTT reduction but with transient neuroinjury/inflammation biomarker elevation; lowest exposure quartile showed 24% mHTT reduction with favorable biomarker profile, demonstrating non-linear exposure-safety relationship and supporting the tominersen paradox

sources.title: WVE-003, an allele-selective antisense oligonucleotide targeting SNP3 to reduce mutant huntingtin while preserving wild-type huntingtin in Huntington's disease
sources.relevance: primary — allele-selective ASO strategy (SNP3 targeting), equivalent potency to non-selective surrogate with WT-huntingtin preservation
sources.key_finding: WVE-003 selectively reduces mHTT by targeting SNP3 (unique to mutant allele) while fully preserving wild-type huntingtin levels; demonstrates equivalent mHTT-lowering potency to non-allele-selective ASO surrogate with improved durability, directly addressing the tominersen paradox

sources.title: The neuropathology of Huntington's disease
sources.relevance: secondary — selective vulnerability cell-type map: MSN (~95% of striatal neurons) >90% degenerate; cholinergic and PV+ interneurons relatively spared; cortical involvement later
sources.key_finding: MSN constitute ~95% of striatal neurons and >90% eventually degenerate in HD; striatal interneurons (cholinergic, calbindin-positive, PV-positive) are relatively preserved through late stages; cortical pyramidal neurons (especially layer V) affected later than striatum; selective vulnerability pattern provides key negative controls for mechanistic hypotheses
